$comment: The tunnel kit (Tileset 04, Tunnel Systems; docs/map-briefs/tunnels/PLAN_2026-11-13.md): one structural shell a shape, material families applied to it. tools/content/kit/tunnel.mjs makes a kit tile for each family and shape (id core.tunnel_<family>_<shape>), and tools/content/tiles.mjs checks and writes them with content/tiles/core.json's. profiles: the clear opening on a cell edge every family keeps (half its width, its clear height, the top of the cap over it), so any two pieces of the same profile meet without a step. families (the first is the one MapMaker's palette shows; `preview`: a family not finished yet, named so in MapMaker's Family select; a placed piece's `family` (map format v37) picks another): materials (library materials: the masses either side, the soffit, the floor, trim, a portal's headwall and wings), lining (how the bore is dressed: haunch = a cast downstand where wall meets soffit, joints = metres between panel joints, arch = a round arch drawn inside the clear box, sets = timber sets and lagging) and trim (plinth height, the floor drain, the pipe run on a straight wall, the strip light at the crown, the hazard band at a mouth, a dead end's door; channel = water drawn between kerbs, never a liquid; rails = a track on sleepers; light.style lantern = a hung lamp; walkway = a raised walkway along each wall (drawn); lanes = carriageway lines (centre dashes, edge lines); guardrail = a rail on each wall; lining.rock = a shell of broken rock drawn inside the clear box (rings every `every` m of `segs` slabs `t` thick, set in by up to `depth`, seeded); rubble = low stones on the floor's edges; stalactites = hung in a chamber; frame = timber on a mouth's face; bars = the outfall's iron). shapes: arms = the sides the passage runs to; mouth = the side a portal opens to the sky (with its headwall and wing walls); door = the side of a dead end's service door; bars = iron bars across a mouth (an outfall: they collide); hatch = a shaft's opening in the cap [x0, z0, x1, z1]; profile = the bore the shape is (S unless it says, the reducer L to the south and S to the north); families = the families a shape comes in, its first the palette's (else every family whose `profiles` include the shape's, in order); doorWidth/doorHeight = a dead end's door size; joint = a transition: this piece's family to the south, the named family to the north (a reducer's: the named family on the wide side), the joint in the middle; collapse = a portal with no headwall (a cave mouth: boulders and a rock slab, its own collision); kind = a piece of more than one cell or level (ramp: one level up over two cells at 1 in 4, for wheels; reducer: L to S in one cell; flight: one level up on steps or a ramp, buried; descent: the same open to the sky, the way down from flat ground; riser: a well between two levels; chamber: a 2 x 2 room). A family changes nothing a player or a bot collides with: trim is drawn only.

concrete.label: Concrete Tunnel
concrete.blurb: Cast concrete with panel joints, a floor drain and a strip light at the crown (utility corridors, culverts, bunkers).

brick.label: Brick Sewer
brick.blurb: Old brick under a round arch, a water channel down the middle between stone kerbs with a grate in each arm, walkways either side, a lantern at the crown (sewers, culverts, old works). The water is drawn only: nothing to wade in.

mine.label: Mine Tunnel
mine.blurb: Rough rock held up by timber sets every 2 m with lagging boards over them, a narrow-gauge track on sleepers down the floor, a lantern hung at the crown (mines, adits, old diggings).

road.label: Road Tunnel
road.blurb: A lined two-lane road: cast panels over an asphalt carriageway with a dashed centre line and edge lines, a raised walkway along each wall behind a wall-mounted guardrail, strip lights at the crown (road tunnels, underpasses, service roads).

cave.label: Cave
cave.blurb: Raw rock: a shell of broken rock lining the passage, rubble on a dirt floor, stalactites in its chambers, no fixtures (natural caves, collapsed diggings; light it with lights).

shapes.blurb: A 3.6 m passage running north–south, buried: the hill stays on top of it.

shapes.name: Curve
shapes.blurb: The passage comes in from the south and turns east.

shapes.name: T-Junction
shapes.blurb: The passage runs east–west with a branch south.

shapes.name: Four-Way
shapes.blurb: Two passages cross.

shapes.name: Dead End
shapes.blurb: The passage comes in from the south and ends at a service door.

shapes.name: Portal
shapes.blurb: The mouth: a headwall, an apron between sloping wing walls (south), the tunnel going on north. It opens the hill and brings the earth to its walls by itself.

shapes.name: Outfall
shapes.blurb: A barred mouth: the portal's headwall, apron and wing walls with iron bars across the opening. Water, light and shots pass; players and bots don't (a culvert's or a sewer's outfall to a creek). For a way in, use the Portal.

shapes.name: Stairs
shapes.blurb: The passage climbs one level on steps, from the south (low) to the north (a level up), buried: the soffit and the earth over it climb with the floor.

shapes.name: Slope
shapes.blurb: The passage climbs one level on a ramp (1 in 2), from the south (low) to the north (a level up), buried like the stairs.

shapes.name: Surface Stairs
shapes.blurb: Steps down from the surface into a tunnel a level under it: open to the sky between low walls, the tunnel going on south at the bottom, the ground at the top (north). The mouth for flat ground.

shapes.name: Shaft
shapes.blurb: A straight passage with a hatch up to the surface over its west wall, a kerb round it and its lid standing open. The ground is brought level to the hatch. It wants a ladder on that wall: the Tunnel Shaft set piece has one.

shapes.name: Riser
shapes.blurb: A capped well joining a passage (south) to one a level up (north). It wants a ladder on the well's north wall: the Tunnel Riser set piece has one.

shapes.name: Chamber
shapes.blurb: A room of 2 x 2 cells (14 m inside) on four columns, a passage-sized opening on each side: south and west in its south-west cell, north in the north-west, east in the south-east. Wall an opening you don't use (Sides), or put a Dead End on it.

shapes.name: Wide
shapes.blurb: A 7 m bore running north–south (profile L: two lanes, vehicles fit), buried: the hill stays on top of it.

shapes.name: Wide Curve
shapes.blurb: The 7 m bore comes in from the south and turns east.

shapes.name: Wide T-Junction
shapes.blurb: The 7 m bore runs east–west with a branch south.

shapes.name: Wide Four-Way
shapes.blurb: Two 7 m bores cross.

shapes.name: Wide Dead End
shapes.blurb: The 7 m bore comes in from the south and ends at a roll-up door.

shapes.name: Wide Portal
shapes.blurb: The 7 m bore's mouth: a headwall, an apron between sloping wing walls (south), the bore going on north. It opens the hill and digs the way in, wide enough for vehicles.

shapes.name: Wide Ramp
shapes.blurb: The 7 m bore climbs one level over two cells (1 in 4, which vehicles drive), from the south (low) to the north (a level up), buried: the soffit and the earth over it climb with the floor.

shapes.name: Reducer
shapes.blurb: Joins the 7 m bore (south) to the 3.6 m passage (north): the walls step in halfway. Vehicles stop at the step; people walk on.

shapes.name: Mouth
shapes.blurb: A cave mouth: no headwall, the hill broken open round the passage, boulders for wings and a slab of rock over the opening (south), the cave going on north. It opens the hill like a portal.

shapes.name: Joint to Cave
shapes.blurb: A transition: the passage in this piece's family to the south, a cave to the north, the joint in the middle (a cast collar with rock breaking over it from concrete, a brick ring from brick, a heavy timber set from a mine).

shapes.name: Joint to Concrete
shapes.blurb: A transition: the passage in this piece's family to the south, concrete to the north, the joint in the middle (an old brick arch into a cast frame with a grate; from a mine, the last timber set against the frame).

shapes.name: Joint to Brick
shapes.blurb: A transition: a mine to the south, a brick sewer to the north, a stone frame at the joint.

shapes.name: Bay to Road
shapes.blurb: A transition: the mine's timber sets (north, the 3.6 m passage) into a lined road bay (south, the 7 m bore) under a roll-up door, rolled up.
